headline: Google DeepMind and Google Cloud will give up to 200 European scientists direct access to their most advanced AI models and science tools, backed by $3 million in computing credits.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a company announcement reported by Reuters, with the same facts from Channel NewsAsia as relayed by UA.NEWS; modest in size, with up to 200 researchers.
importance_line: European researchers who win a place get tools and computing time they might otherwise lack, which matters to universities and to Google's standing with scientists, but the scheme is capped at 200 researchers and the report does not say how they will be chosen or how the credits are shared.
summary: Reuters reports from Brussels that Google DeepMind, Google's AI research lab, and Google Cloud, Alphabet's cloud service, will give up to 200 European researchers direct access to their frontier models and science tools, including AlphaFold 3, WeatherNext, AlphaGenome and AlphaEvolve, together with $3 million in compute credits. The companies said the access should help scientists tackle complex problems, such as predicting extreme weather and mapping molecular structures, faster.
notes: Reuters site returned HTTP 401; the text was read in Central Oregon Daily's carried copy of the Reuters wire, and the Reuters link is kept. Channel NewsAsia gives the same facts (read as relayed by UA.NEWS).
